public_rationale: Skepticism about scaling alone had become a widely accepted position: the AAAI survey reported substantial majority skepticism, and a prominent industry scientist publicly endorsed it. Scaling optimists nevertheless remained influential. The evidence supports the ordinary reading of mainstream as a substantial, established position; it does not support unanimity or prove the underlying forecast.
limitations: The survey was academically weighted and was not a representative industry poll.
Support depends on reading mainstream as broadly accepted rather than universally or overwhelmingly accepted across industry.
Respondents expressed likelihood judgments, not a proof of impossibility.

statement.excerpt: The notion on which this Substack was founded in May 2022 — that LLM scaling would not bring us to AGI — has gone mainstream.
statement.document_title: The bad news: AI is going pretty much as I expected

from_speaker: LLM scaling would not bring us to AGI
our_interpretation: Mainstream means a widely accepted position in the AI research and industry debate, without requiring unanimity or agreement from every leading laboratory.
The observation concerns public acceptance of skepticism, not whether that skepticism is technically correct.
There is no regular reporting period for this public debate. I use the current reporting year through publication, January 1 to September 5, 2025.
The survey's public reporting date establishes its entry into the debate; it does not establish when every respondent formed that opinion.
criteria.support_condition: A substantial researcher survey showing broad skepticism, corroborated by prominent industry positions during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that skepticism remained a fringe position in the relevant research and industry debate.
